sentences.text: Skorpiovenator is classified as a fairly large member of the abelisaurid dinosaur family.
The preserved portion of the type specimen measures 4.35 meters from the premaxilla to the 12th tail vertebra.
Based on the anatomy of related species, the animal is estimated to have reached a total length of 6 to 6.2 meters and a weight of slightly under 900 kilograms.
It possessed a short, blunt skull that resembled that of Carnotaurus.
The skull measured 54.1 cm in length from the premaxilla to the quadrate.
The postorbital bone was large and intersected the eye socket, nearly touching the opposite lacrimal bone.
Skorpiovenator had four teeth in each premaxilla and 19 teeth in each maxilla, a count higher than in any other abelisaurid.
Its thin jaws held several sharp teeth with serrated edges.
Although the arms and scapulae were not found, they are assumed to have been short like in related species.
The name references the abundance of scorpions found at the excavation site.
The species name bustingorryi honors Manuel Bustingorry, the farm owner who died before the species was formally described.
The type specimen was discovered in 2005 by paleontologists Juan Ignacio Canale and Agustín Scanferla.
The type specimen of Skorpiovenator was formally described in 2009 and is considered one of the most complete abelisaurid skeletons known.
The holotype specimen (MMCH-PV 48) is housed in the Municipal Museum "Ernesto Bachmann" in Villa El Chocón, Neuquén, Argentina.
Skorpiovenator was formally described and named by Canale, Scanferla, Agnolin, and Novas in 2009, though the description article was digitally pre-published in 2008.
A detailed description of the skull anatomy was published by Canale et al. in 2026.
Researchers suggest Skorpiovenator may have used its high skull like a mace, swinging it backward against prey so its teeth could penetrate with enough force to cause damage.
Skorpiovenator shared its Late Cretaceous habitat with giant sauropods like Argentinosaurus and other dinosaurs such as Choconsaurus and Chucarosaurus.
It likely lived at the same time as other carnivores including the carcharodontosaurid Mapusaurus and the abelisaurid Ilokelesia.
The genus Skorpiovenator was established by Canale et al. in 2008.
The species Skorpiovenator bustingorryi was described by Canale et al. in 2008.
In 2009, Canale et al. placed Skorpiovenator within the subclade Brachyrostra, a group of short-snouted Carnotaurinae.
Researchers suggest that isolated teeth previously assigned to Carcharodontosauridae actually belong to abelisaurids based on similarities with Skorpiovenator's teeth.
Skorpiovenator was an abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) period.
Fossils of Skorpiovenator were found in the Huincul Formation in Neuquén, Patagonia, Argentina.
The Huincul Formation, where Skorpiovenator fossils are found, is estimated to be 106.2 million years old.
Skorpiovenator lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
The fossil strata containing the type specimen are now dated to the late Albian stage, approximately 106.2 million years ago.
Skorpiovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 95 and 93 million years ago, in the Cenomanian stage.
